result.target_topic: Transition to EUV lithography and capital intensity
result.target_summary: Intel transitioned from non-EUV to EUV lithography with Intel 4 and Intel 3 process nodes in 2024, which drives higher capital investment compared to preceding technologies. Semiconductor manufacturing is capital-intensive, with 2024 manufacturing capex distributed 55% to facility space and 45% to equipment, inclusive of technology development.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
D050 (2023) details factory operations, ramping new process technologies, and supply chain capacity. D049 (2024) details the status of specific process nodes (Intel 7, 4, 3) and their high-volume manufacturing locations (Arizona, Israel, Ireland). Both focus on the operational execution and status of manufacturing nodes.

Both disclosures discuss capital-intensive manufacturing, facility/equipment distribution, and the transition to advanced lithography (EUV) requiring significant investment. D050 highlights supply chain/minimizing disruptions in 2023, while D052 in 2024 details the EUV transition and capex split (55% facility, 45% equipment) driven by this new technology.

comparisons.peer_summary: R&D expenses vary primarily with the number of wafers processed, personnel costs, and the cost of advanced equipment, such as EUV lithography investments.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron explicitly identify EUV lithography equipment as a significant driver of capital intensity and R&D expenses. Intel discloses that the transition to EUV with Intel 4 and Intel 3 nodes drives higher capital investment compared to preceding technologies, while Micron states that R&D expenses vary with the cost of advanced equipment dedicated to new product and process development, such as investments in EUV lithography equipment.

sentences.text: In 2024, we made the transition from non-EUV lithography to EUV lithography with the Intel 4 and Intel 3 process nodes.
EUV lithography equipment drives a higher capital investment than the preceding lithography technology.

R&D expenses vary primarily with the number of development and pre-qualification wafers processed and end-product solutions developed, personnel costs, and the cost of advanced equipment dedicated to new product and process development, such as investments in EUV lithography equipment.

comparisons.peer_topic: Global manufacturing footprint and subcontractor use
comparisons.peer_summary: Products are manufactured in own facilities across seven countries and utilize subcontractors for certain processes.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies explicitly characterize semiconductor manufacturing as a capital-intensive industry requiring large investments in facilities and equipment. Intel details that 2024 manufacturing capex was distributed 55% to facility space and 45% to equipment, while Micron states that manufacturing is capital-intensive, requiring large investments in sophisticated facilities and equipment.

sentences.text: Semiconductor manufacturing is a capital-intensive industry.

Over the past four years, we have made outsized investments across three categories-technology development, manufacturing facility shells, and advanced production tools-as we aim to catch up with our leading third-party manufacturing competitor on process technology, get to "shell ahead" for our and potential future foundry customer needs, and adopt EUV lithography for our leading process nodes.
In 2024, our manufacturing capital expenditures, inclusive of technology development, were distributed 55% in manufacturing facility space and 45% in equipment.
Semiconductor manufacturing is capital intensive, requiring large investments in sophisticated facilities and equipment.
